newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in moderate trade on Friday, dealers said.

They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. July employment report, June personal income/consumption, June factory orders and July National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) index data.
In the July employment report, payroll jobs were expected to be around 193,000 compared with 217,000 jobs reported in June.
The unemployment rate is expected to dip to 4.9 percent against 5.0 percent.
Personal income for June is expected to rise to 0.4 percent from May's 0.3 percent and June's personal consumption is expected to rise to 0.4 percent versus May's 0.3 percent.
Factory orders for June is expected to rise to 1.5 percent against a 0.7 percent decline in May.
The July NAPM index is expected to rise to 56.1 percent from June's 55.7 percent.

"The market is waiting for tonight's release of the (July) employment report, (June) personal income/consumption, (June) factory orders and (July) NAPM index figures, for fresh direction," a local dealer said.
"But I don't think there will be much impact as the numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared their positions for the weekend," he said.
In day-to-day rates, weekend eased 1/16 percentage point to 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent. Monday/Tuesday and week-fixed were unchanged from Thursday's common 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged from Thursday's 5-5/8 5-1/2 pecent, three-months unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16, nine-months eased 1/16 point to 5-13/16 5-11/16 and twelve-months was unchanged at 5-15/16 5-13/16 percent.
